relative.sentence: I bought a new phone ___ has a great camera.
The woman ___ lives next door is a doctor.
That's the man ___ car was stolen.
This is the town ___ I grew up.
Sunday is the day ___ I relax.
I don't know the reason ___ she left.
Peter, with ___ I spoke yesterday, was very helpful.
Peter, ___ I spoke with yesterday, was very helpful.
relative.explanation: Sin preposición delante → who (la preposición va al final).

relative.sentence: My grandfather, on ___ I rely a lot, is 90.
Maria, to ___ I sent the email, hasn't answered.
Avatar, ___ is my favourite film, was great.
The film ___ I saw yesterday was great. (defining)
Which sentence is a NON-defining relative clause?
options: My car, which is red, is very fast.
The car that I bought is very fast.
The man who called is my boss.
The book I read was boring.
relative.answer: My car, which is red, is very fast.

relative.sentence: In which sentence can the relative pronoun be omitted?
options: The film that I saw yesterday was great.
The man who called you is my boss.
Avatar, which is my favourite film, was great.
The girl who won is my sister.
relative.answer: The film that I saw yesterday was great.
relative.explanation: Se omite cuando es O.D. de una defining (detrás hay sujeto: I).

relative.sentence: Which sentence is WRONG?
options: Avatar, that is my favourite film, was great.
Avatar, which is my favourite film, was great.
The film that I saw was great.
The film I saw was great.
relative.answer: Avatar, that is my favourite film, was great.
relative.explanation: En non-defining no se puede usar that.

relative.sentence: The students ___ passed the exam got a prize. (someone)
My sister, ___ lives in Madrid, is coming tomorrow.
The house ___ Peter painted is mine. (escribe that o which)
relative.explanation: Defining: that / which (también se puede omitir).

relative.sentence: That's the girl ___ father is a famous actor.

___ home, I saw an accident.
___ at home, I felt sick.

___ for the job, I waited for a call.
___ at a low temperature, the meat would taste better.

participle.explanation: Instead of a relative clause: quitamos who + is.

participle.sentence: I found Peter ___ in the exam.
I saw my brother ___ on the phone.
___ his homework, he went out with his friends.
Which sentence is correct?
options: Cooked at a low temperature, the meat tastes better.
Studied this in detail, you will find it interesting.
Cooking at a low temperature, the meat tastes better.
Having cooked at a low temperature, the meat tastes better.
participle.answer: Cooked at a low temperature, the meat tastes better.
participle.explanation: If → MV-ed2: 1ª parte pasiva y mismo sujeto (the meat).

participle.sentence: Which sentence is WRONG?
options: Studied more, you will pass the test.
Wanting to pass, I studied a lot.
Driving home, I saw an accident.
Having applied for the job, I waited.
participle.answer: Studied more, you will pass the test.
participle.explanation: 'You' no es estudiado: la 1ª parte no es pasiva.

options: that are called Peter and Mike
that is a very strict woman
that is the capital of Spain
